night.e: How do you sleep at night when you attack your kids like that!?

nineteen.d: The cardinal number occurring after eighteen and before twenty, represented in Roman numerals as XIX and in Arabic numerals as 19. It is the last/largest of the "teens".

ninety.d: The cardinal number occurring after eighty-nine and before ninety-one, represented in Roman numerals as XC and in Arabic numerals as 90.

no.d: A negating expression; an answer that shows disagreement or disapproval
no.e: I just want to find out whether she's coming or no. (Scotland)

noise.d: Various sounds, usually unwanted or unpleasant.
noise.e: He knew that it was trash day, when the garbage collectors made all the noise.

nose.d: A protuberance on the face housing the nostrils, which are used to breathe or smell.
nose.e: She had a small nose between two sparkling blue eyes.

not.d: A unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true.
not.e: Did you take out the trash? No, I did not.

note.e: If you look to the left, you can note the old cathedral.

notebook.d: A book (physical or digital) in which notes or memoranda are written.

nothing.e: Don't just say nothing. Tell me what's going on.

november.d: Alternative letter-case form of November from the NATO/ICAO Phonetic Alphabet.

number.e: Any number of people can be reading from a given repository at a time.

o'clock.d: (modifying a numeral, one to twelve) In conjunction with a numeral, indicates the time within a twelve-hour period (midnight to noon or noon to midnight), specifically the time when the hour hand of a clock points precisely to the symbol or marking corresponding to the designated numeral.

off.d: (usually in phrases such as 'from the off', 'at the off', etc.) Beginning; starting point.
off.e: He has been very obviously an untrustworthy narrator right from the off.

office.d: A ceremonial duty or service, particularly:
office.e: When the office of Secretary of State is vacant, its duties fall upon an official within the department.

often.e: I often walk to work when the weather is nice.

old.d: Of an object, concept, relationship, etc., having existed for a relatively long period of time.

once.e: I have only once eaten pizza.

one.d: The number represented by the Arabic numeral 1; the numerical value equal to that cardinal number.
one.e: In some religions, there is more than one god.

open.d: Physically unobstructed, uncovered, etc. Able to have something pass through or along it.

opera.d: A theatrical work, combining drama, music, song and sometimes dance; usually, one sung-through, based on classical music and seen as more artistic and formalized than other forms of musical theater.

or.d: Connects at least two alternative words, phrases, clauses, sentences, etc. each of which could make a passage true. In English, this is the "inclusive or." The "exclusive or" is formed by "either [...] or".
or.e: He might get cancer, or be hit by a bus, or God knows what.

orange.d: An evergreen tree of the genus Citrus such as Citrus sinensis.

other.e: Pick up the phone and find out who's on the other end.

our.d: Belonging to us, excluding the person(s) being addressed .
our.e: Sorry, you're not invited to our party.

ours.d: That or those belonging to us. Excluding the person(s) being addressed
ours.e: You can't take that! It's ours!

out.d: A means of exit, escape, reprieve, etc.
out.e: They wrote the law to give those organizations an out.

outside.d: The part of something that faces out; the outer surface.
outside.e: He's repainting the outside of his house.

over.e: The show isn't over until the fat lady sings.

own.d: Belonging to; possessed; proper to. Often marks a possessive determiner as reflexive, referring back to the subject of the clause or sentence.
own.e: When we move into the new house, the kids will each have their own bedroom.

owner.e: The police recovered the stolen car and returned it to its owner.

p.m..d: In the 12-hour period from noon to midnight (the latter half of the day) when using the 12-hour clock.

page.d: One of the many pieces of paper bound together within a book or similar document.
page.e: The book which he was reading had 213 pages.

paint.d: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds color/colour to an object or surface to which it has been applied.

painting.e: The outside of the old house would benefit from some painting.

pair.d: Two similar or identical things taken together; often followed by of.
pair.e: I couldn't decide which of the pair of designer shirts I preferred, so I bought the pair.

palace.d: Official residence of a head of state or other dignitary, especially in a monarchical or imperial governmental system.

pants.d: An outer garment that covers the body from the waist downwards, covering each leg separately, usually as far as the ankles; trousers.
pants.e: The pants are fine, but the jacket will have to be altered.

paper.d: A sheet material typically used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
paper.e: Draw on the paper! Not on the walls!

paragraph.d: A passage in text that starts on a new line, the first line sometimes being indented, and usually marks a change of topic.

parent.d: A person who raises a child (which they have made, adopted, fostered, taken as their own, etc.).
parent.e: After both her parents were killed in a forest fire, Sonia was adopted by her aunt and uncle.

park.d: An area of land set aside for environment preservation or recreation.
park.e: Let's park that until next week's meeting.

partner.d: Someone who is associated with another in a common activity or interest.

party.d: A person or group of people constituting one side in a legal proceeding, such as in a legal action or a contract.
party.e: The contract requires that the party of the first part pay the fee.

past.d: The period of time that has already happened, in contrast to the present and the future.
past.e: a book about a time machine that can transport people back into the past

pay.d: Money given in return for work; salary or wages.

peace.d: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony; absence of violence. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance.
peace.e: Our lounge strives to maintain an environment of peace for the comfort of our customers.

pen.d: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
pen.e: There are two steers in the third pen.

pencil.d: A writing utensil with a graphite (commonly referred to as lead) shaft, usually blended with clay, clad in wood, and sharpened to a taper.
pencil.e: I penciled (BrE: pencilled) a brief reminder in my notebook.

people.d: Used as plural of person; a body of human beings considered generally or collectively; a group of two or more persons.
people.e: There were so many people at the restaurant last night.

person.d: An individual who has been granted personhood; usually a human being.
person.e: Each person is unique, both mentally and physically.

personal.d: Pertaining to persons (human beings as opposed to things or animals).

pet.d: An animal kept as a companion.
pet.e: The professor seemed offended by the criticism of her pet theory.

phone.d: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.

piano.d: A percussive keyboard musical instrument, usually ranging over seven octaves, with white and black colored keys, played by pressing these keys, causing hammers to strike strings
piano.e: He can play "Happy Birthday" on the piano.

pick.d: A tool used for digging; a pickaxe.

picture.d: A representation of anything (as a person, a landscape, a building) upon canvas, paper, or other surface, by drawing, painting, printing, photography, etc.

piece.d: A part of a larger whole, usually in such a form that it is able to be separated from other parts.
piece.e: I’d like another piece of pie.

pig.d: Any of several mammalian species of the family Suidae, having cloven hooves, bristles and a snout adapted for digging; especially the domesticated animal Sus domesticus.
pig.e: The man kept a pen with two pigs that he fed everything from carrots to cabbage.

pizza.d: A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread dough crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese and other ingredients such as meat, vegetables or fruit
pizza.e: Want to go out for pizza tonight?

place.d: (physical) An area; somewhere within an area.

plan.d: A drawing showing technical details of a building, machine, etc., with unwanted details omitted, and often using symbols rather than detailed drawing to represent doors, valves, etc.
plan.e: He didn't really have a plan; he had a goal and a habit of control.

play.d: Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.

player.d: One that plays. One who plays any game or sport.
player.e: He is a player for the Australian team.

please.d: To make happy or satisfy; to give pleasure to.

pleasure.d: A state of being pleased or contented; gratification.
pleasure.e: He remembered with pleasure his home and family.

pocket.d: A bag stitched to an item of clothing, used for carrying small items.
pocket.e: I paid for it out of my own pocket.

pollution.d: The desecration of something holy or sacred; defilement, profanation.

poor.d: (with "the") Those who have little or no possessions or money, taken as a group.
poor.e: The poor are always with us.

pop.d: A loud, sharp sound, as of a cork coming out of a bottle, especially when the contents are pressurized by fizziness.
pop.e: Listen to the pop of a champagne cork.

post.d: A long dowel or plank protruding from the ground; a fencepost; a lightpost.
post.e: ram a post into the ground

potato.d: The tuber of a plant, Solanum tuberosum, eaten as a starchy vegetable, particularly in the Americas and Europe; this plant.

present.d: The current moment or period of time.
present.e: The barbaric practice continues to the present day.

pretty.d: A pretty person; a term of address to a pretty person.
pretty.e: We'll stop at the knife store and look at the sharp pretties.

price.d: The cost required to gain possession of something.
price.e: I paid a high price for my folly.

prince.d: A (male) ruler, a sovereign; a king, monarch.

princess.d: A female member of a royal family other than a queen, especially a daughter or granddaughter.

problem.d: A difficulty that has to be resolved or dealt with.
problem.e: She's leaving because she faced numerous problems to do with racism.

program.e: Our program for today’s exercise class includes swimming and jogging.

programme.d: UK, New Zealand, and India standard spelling of program.
programme.e: Our programme for today’s exercise class includes swimming and jogging.

purple.d: A colour/color that is a dark blend of red and blue; dark magenta.

push.d: A short, directed application of force; an act of pushing.
push.e: Give the door a hard push if it sticks.

put.d: A right to sell something at a predetermined price.
put.e: He bought a January '08 put for Procter and Gamble at 80 to hedge his bet.

question.d: A sentence, phrase or word which asks for information, reply or response; an interrogative.

quickly.d: Rapidly; with speed; fast; with expedition.
quickly.e: Luckily, the error was quickly corrected.

quiet.e: There was a strange quiet in the normally very lively plaza.

rabbit.d: A mammal of most genera of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail. (Those of the larger kind are instead called hares)
rabbit.e: She was cooking rabbit stew for dinner.

radio.d: The technology that allows for the transmission of sound or other signals by modulation of electromagnetic waves.

rain.d: Condensed water falling from a cloud.

rainy.e: Due to the rainy weather, we decided not to play in the park.

rat.d: Any of the numerous members of several rodent families that usually have short limbs, a pointy snout, a long, hairless tail, and a body length greater than about 12 cm, or 5 inches.
rat.e: He ratted a vertical line on his face with a pocket knife.

read.d: A reading or an act of reading, especially an actor's part of a play.
read.e: His thrillers are always a gripping read.

reader.e: an early reader, a talented reader
